title: Canonical CI exact pull-request head identity

phases.objective: Bind every canonical CI checkout and deployment-evidence identity to the exact pull-request head so governed Production candidates are never evaluated through GitHub's synthetic merge commit.

e2e_journeys.actor: GitHub Actions pull-request runner and repository reviewer
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A same-repository pull request targeting main or Production triggers .github/workflows/ci.yml.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: All four canonical CI jobs check out the exact pull-request head, deployment evidence records that same identity, and the regression test rejects any return to a synthetic merge checkout without granting write or runtime authority.
steps: Resolve the pull-request head SHA, with github.sha retained only for non-pull-request events.
Checkout that exact identity with complete history in Syntax, Unit and Integration, Architecture Drift, and Execution Resolver jobs.
Run the existing Production promotion classifier and Context Kernel scope logic against the checked-out candidate.
Bind DEPLOYMENT_COMMIT_SHA to the same exact identity before producing read-only deployment evidence.
Execute the CI recovery self-test to prove four canonical exact-head checkout blocks and one exact deployment identity binding.
assertions: Canonical CI contains exactly four exact-head checkout blocks.
Canonical deployment evidence is bound to the exact pull-request head.
Recovery retains its two exact-head checkout blocks.
No synthetic merge identity is introduced as candidate evidence.
No contents write, protected-ref mutation, deployment, provider call, database action, migration, credential access, external send, or force push is introduced.

phases.objective: Expose the verified exact checkout identity as a typed field across canonical CI progress reports.
Prove exact identity preservation across pull-request synchronize, rerun, push, and workflow-dispatch event families.
This CI identity correction has no provider or runtime canary authority.
This CI identity correction grants no Production merge or deployment authority.
